chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'They slept little of the night.' He said: 'They slept the fewest nights; they did not rise [for prayer] in them.'

key_terms.تَفُوتُهُمْ: they miss or are lacking in them
key_terms.يَهْجَعُونَ: to sleep or lie down to rest

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'They slept little of the night' mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the phrase 'they slept little of the night' as a reference to the righteous who missed night prayer on only a few occasions, thereby emphasizing the consistency of the pious in *Qiyam al-Layl*. This explanation underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the regularity of night worship as a distinguishing trait of the *Salihun*, linking spiritual vigilance directly to the quality of one's devotion.
